source.title: A second-order-like optimizer with adaptive gradient scaling for deep learning
source.authors: Jérôme Bolte; Ryan Boustany; Edouard Pauwels; Andrei Purica

record.file_problem: Full paper and appendix text supplied; some figures are represented only by plotted curves, and no exact values can be read from them here.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own optimizer comparisons on natural-label image classification and language tasks, including training and held-out metrics, and finds that outcomes depend on optimizer settings and training duration. It does not test memorization of random labels or the broader architecture, size, and generalization-measure claims.
record.gate_note: The CIFAR-10, ImageNet, Food101, and GPT-2 results compare INNAprop with AdamW and report training and held-out performance. Random-label memorization, interpolation, architecture comparisons, and generalization measures are not tested. The paper's optimizer results bear on the optimizer-related scope of V4; the V4 version's specific comparison of adaptive methods with SGD is not performed.
record.test_reason: The study benchmarks a new optimizer against AdamW and discusses a convergence–generalization trade-off, citing Wilson et al. It does not test any specified version. In particular, comparisons between adaptive optimizers do not establish V4's adaptive-versus-SGD difference, its recovery through broader tuning, or its recovery through decoupled weight decay or switching optimizers. Appendix F.5 compares against INNA, not SGD or momentum SGD.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate as a summary of the authors' conclusion: they present INNAprop as matching or exceeding AdamW across their benchmarks, with strong early-training gains and parameter choices that affect convergence speed and final accuracy. This is an author conclusion about their optimizer, not evidence for the specified adaptive-versus-SGD claim.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces and evaluates INNAprop, a new optimizer combining INNA dynamics with RMSprop scaling; compares it mainly with AdamW. It does not use the original claim's random-label, width, architecture, or sharpness experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: CIFAR-10 outcomes vary with INNAprop friction parameters (α, β) and training duration; image-classification recommendations differ between shorter and longer training. GPT-2 configuration uses σ = 0.99 for pretraining and σ = 0.999 for LoRA fine-tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: INNAprop's reported held-out metrics improve on AdamW across the tabulated image and language benchmarks; these are comparisons of the proposed adaptive optimizer with another adaptive optimizer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: INNAprop can match or improve AdamW's held-out performance under the tested training recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-10, the authors report that faster INNAprop configurations generally generalize worse than slower configurations. Section 3.2 also describes lower ImageNet ResNet50 test accuracy for the faster configuration.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: INNAprop's convergence-speed and held-out-performance trade-off depends on its friction parameters and training duration.

record.peer_reviewed: Trans. Mach. Learn. Res.; text also says preprint under review
record.problems: Optimizer comparison is not a direct test of V4's adaptive-versus-SGD claim. Authors state AdamW was systematically favored in hyperparameter choices and INNAprop received minimal large-scale tuning due to constrained computational resources. Several plots provide no textual numerical values; ImageNet ViT-B/32 results use one run.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under limited tuning; recovery through broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, or switching to SGD; Adam versus SGD on word-level language models.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and removal of dropout with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Change V4 from tested_not_extracted to not tested. All rows remain unlinked; cannot_determine denotes their inability to establish a claim-version effect, not unreadability of the tabulated numbers. The supplied text identifies itself as a preprint under review and does not substantiate the record's TMLR publication status.

versions.untested_parts: No fixed random labels, random-label test accuracy, or natural-label versus random-label comparison.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
Tests optimizer effects on training and held-out performance, but does not compare Adam or other adaptive optimizers against SGD or momentum SGD as stated in this version.
No batch-size comparison or fixed-epoch large-batch penalty analysis.
No dropout intervention or comparison of dropout and weight decay.
No sharpness or other generalization measure.

relation.reason: Remark 4 discusses convergence speed and generalization, citing Wilson et al.; the experiments do not test a specified version.

tranche.reason: The benchmarks compare INNAprop with adaptive optimizers, chiefly AdamW, and neither test nor use any specified claim version. The convergence–generalization discussion does not establish V4's adaptive-versus-SGD result.

source_check.notes: These are own-method benchmarks outside the claim versions; language-model validation loss and test perplexity are relevant held-out measures, but the SGD comparison is missing. Source inconsistencies remain: Food101 epochs and learning rate in Appendix G.2 conflict with Section 3.2; ViT run counts differ between Figure 3 and Table 3; ResNet50 parameters in Table 3 differ from the surrounding figure discussion.
